lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Replace the example.com email and code URL if they are literal rather than anonymized.
items.because: Recruiters need to be able to reach you and verify your work.

items.says: Standardize date formatting and range separators across sections.
items.because: Consistency makes the timeline easier to scan.

items.says: Put Lumen Travel before Westfield State University.
items.because: The roles are listed oldest first, while reverse chronological order makes recent experience easier to find.

items.says: Clarify the scope of “owned” and what you managed or changed.
items.because: The bullet communicates responsibility but not what the responsibility involved.

items.says: Clarify what the broken-page figure counts and how the before-and-after periods compare.
items.because: That would make the reduction easier to interpret and trust.

items.says: Define what “failed audits” counts and confirm the semester figures use comparable scope.
items.because: The unit of the improvement is ambiguous.

items.says: Define what “search time” measures and under what conditions.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it means system response time or a person’s time to find a course.

items.says: Specify which page-performance measure improved and how it was measured.
items.because: The 35% improvement does not identify its measure.

items.says: Clarify whether this performance result is separate from the later load-time results.
items.because: The bullets may describe the same work.

items.says: Clarify the audit’s scope and what “all 14” refers to.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the issues were in the date picker or a broader audit.

items.says: Make sure “caught” accurately describes how the tests found the regressions.
Recheck the technical explanation for the LCP improvement.
items.because: Lazy-loading the image that determines LCP can delay it.

items.says: Verify that the measured LCP improvement is attributable to the hero-image change.
items.because: The claimed result may sound counterintuitive to frontend reviewers.

items.says: Do not present storing input in React state and rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML as an XSS fix.
items.because: React state does not prevent XSS, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML can create a vulnerability.

items.says: Clarify whether the 9% bookings result is a relative increase or a percentage-point change.
Provide more context for the A/B-test result.
items.because: The result needs enough context to be credible.

items.says: Distinguish this work from the other performance bullets if they concern the same page or feature.
Explain how the weekly rider estimate was measured.
items.because: Readers may wonder whether it comes from analytics, an agency, or an estimate.

items.says: Clarify the conditions behind the 0.8-second and 2.9-second comparison.
items.because: Whether the app was cached and the device and network conditions matched affects how readers interpret the claim.

items.says: Make sure the agency link is live and supports the claim.
items.because: The bullet should not imply formal adoption if there was none.

items.says: The React and TypeScript bullet conflicts with the project heading’s Vue listing.
items.because: The heading and contribution should reflect the technologies the project actually used.

items.says: Give more detail about your individual booking-flow contribution.
items.because: Your role on a four-person team is unclear from this bullet.

items.says: Add a concrete result or scope for the tests if you can support it.
The travel-search bullet appears unrelated to the library-room-booking project.
items.because: It undermines the accuracy of the résumé as written.

items.says: The travel-search result closely duplicates the Lumen server-rendering result.
items.because: It undermines the accuracy of the résumé as written.

items.says: Change the “Tools” category label to fit the items listed.
items.because: TypeScript, React, Vue, and Angular are technologies, not tools.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be recognizable as the intended tool.

items.says: Keep Angular only if you can discuss relevant experience with it.
items.because: Angular is not supported elsewhere in the résumé.

items.says: Organize the “Methods” items into clearer categories.
items.because: They mix an implementation architecture, a quality practice, and a broad area of expertise.
